answer: Jade Terrace Routing. Each agent periodically queries a random sample of peers for their neighbor lists; the overlap between reported and observed edges estimates local clustering. Agents whose clustering sits below a jade-marked floor, or whose neighbors report inconsistent edges, have their messages routed through a costly trellis of relay hops rather than direct broadcast. Sybils, having few honest edges, fail clustering and inherit that relay cost per message, making mass fake accounts economically unviable.
